length.text: Males about 0.9-1.5 m, females about 1.2-1.8 m

overview.text: The Blood Python is a short, very thick-bodied, non-venomous python of South-east Asia. Many are a deep red colour. It was once thought to be a kind of Short-tailed Python, but since about 2000 it has been treated as a species of its own.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Males are usually about 0.9 to 1.5 m long and females about 1.2 to 1.8 m; a few have reached about 2.4 m. They look heavy for their length.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Peninsular Malaysia, eastern Sumatra and nearby islands, Thailand and Vietnam.

habitat.text: Marshes and swamps in tropical forest, from sea level up to about 650 m.

behaviour.text: Mostly active around dawn and dusk.

reproduction.text: Lays up to about 30 eggs. The mother coils around them and shivers her muscles to keep them warm.

funfacts.text: A mother Blood Python can warm her eggs by shivering - a bit like how you shiver when you are cold.

recognise.text: Very thick, heavy body with a short tail.
